name: Dutch Marquise
definition: A Dutch Marquise is an elongated hexagonal cut diamond: a long, narrow marquise-style silhouette whose long edges carry angular points, tapering toward each end of its length rather than ending in a flat edge. It is a trade name, not an officially recognized gemological shape, listed on a grading report as a hexagonal modified brilliant.
outline: Elongated hexagon: a long, narrow marquise-style silhouette whose long edges carry angular points, tapering toward each end of its length rather than ending in a flat edge.
end_treatment: The long edges carry angular points that make the outline read as a hexagon rather than a smooth marquise, tapering toward each end of the length.
faceting_status: Brilliant style: symmetrical facets arranged to maximize sparkle and fire. The Elongated Hexagon shares the outline and is the step cut of the pair.

measured_examples.source: Stienhardt reference stone, IGI report measurements
measured_examples.note: length divided by width in millimeters

length_to_width_ratio.note: No standardized ratio exists; this specification publishes measured values only.

durability_notes: The pointed ends are the most exposed part of any elongated outline; a setting that protects the tips (V-prongs or a bezel at the points) is standard practice. Wear behavior depends on the individual stone.

provenance.claim_scope: We publish this plain, repeatable definition of the Dutch Marquise, and Stienhardt controls this cut through a specialized factory relationship and hand-sets and finishes the stones in New York City.
provenance.claim_boundary: We did not invent, patent, or trademark the Dutch Marquise. The term predates this definition as a loose label for a hexagonal diamond with no fixed proportions.

sources.claim: Dutch Marquise is a trade name with no official gemological recognition.
sources.source: Solitaire Lab Diamond, Dutch Marquise Diamond

sources.claim: Grading laboratories describe the geometry rather than printing the trade name; an IGI report for a Stienhardt Dutch Marquise reads Hexagonal Modified Brilliant.
Measured reference ratio 1.84 (length divided by width from the report measurements).

sources.claim: The Dutch Marquise is cut for brilliance; the Elongated Hexagon is the step cut of the pair.
